Outline

  1. Shortcomings of the previous environmentwhat was wrong, in plain terms

FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v22

Shortcomings of the previous environment

  1. Valuation fields were tied to the hidden value by a fixed formula
  2. Phases started on the same day in every run
  3. Volatility did not cluster and had no fat tails
  4. The crash-severity setting changed outcomes by under 1 pp
  5. Volume, sentiment and implied volatility followed the phase label
  6. Every run started 100 % in cash, and SELL did nothing on day 1
  7. Target cash levels 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.2 were stipulated
  8. The prompt showed 10 of the 16 listed fields; no baselines, no cost model
FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v23
Change 1

Price = value × mispricing

log P = log V + x, one stated equation for every scenario
  • Value V: an exogenous random walk with fat-tailed shocks, about 6.5 % a year drift and 0.6 % daily volatility
  • Mispricing x: generated by a separate process (next slides)
  • Price is the product of the two; the agent sees P, never V or x
Why value and price come from separate processes, so the ground truth is explicit and can never be recovered from an accounting identity
FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v24
Change 2

Valuation fields no longer pin down the value

  • Earnings: quarterly, reported 25–35 days late, 10 % noise, and a hidden multiple per run (14–22)
  • P/E is trailing four quarters; dividends are sticky; the analyst estimate carries a persistent 15 % error
Why the signals still point the right way when mispricing is large, but no formula on the shown fields reproduces V
Best formula on shown fieldsBeforeAfter
multiple × price ÷ P/E, median error vs V0.2 %15 %
analyst fair-value estimate, error vs V—22 %
grey line = perfect reconstruction; a hidden multiple and lagged earnings turn the line into a cloud
FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v25
Change 3

Mispricing with a published form

  • Calm phases: Franke–Westerhoff fundamentalists (pull towards value) and chartists (extrapolate), driven by one innovation
  • Persistence: stationary half-life ≈ 150 days (≈ 70 days realised), a stated design value
  • Re-estimation on 10 US stocks was attempted; return moments do not identify the persistence, so the published form is used and the published index parameters are kept as a sensitivity
Why mispricing now persists, so even the flat market contains decisions that are right or wrong
FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v26
Change 4

Real volatility dynamics

  • One innovation process: GJR-GARCH(1,1) with Student-t(5) shocks and rare jumps (1 % of days, −4 % ± 3 %)
  • Persistence 0.98; event phases scale the variance (panic ×5, post-top ×3, mania ×1.5)
Why clustering, fat tails and crash asymmetry become properties of the series; the old artificial mean-reversion signal is gone
FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v27
Change 5

Events scripted in direction, random in timing

  • Each run draws its own setup length (25–55 % of the horizon), panic length (15–70 days), crash depth (10–30 %) and discount (55 / 70 / 85 %)
  • Bubbles: compounding drift, a probabilistic top (about half of runs top inside the horizon, peak P/V ≈ 2.1) and a post-top leg
  • Sustained-bull control; event-first and phase-free orderings as further controls
Why the phase cannot be read from the calendar; severity now matters; topped and un-topped bubbles are two reported populations
FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v28
Change 6

Observables follow the market, not the label

  • Sentiment: autoregressive, driven by current mispricing and recent returns
  • Volume: rises with |return| and |mispricing|
  • Implied volatility: 21-day GARCH forecast plus a premium that depends on the volatility state
  • Technicals: SMA 20/50, Wilder RSI, MACD with signal, checked against a reference library
Why no field is computed from the phase label, so none of them is a phase clock
FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v29
Change 7

Start allocation and action are design factors

  • Start: the persona's band centre (primary), a common 50 % cash, or 100 % cash as a bridge to the old results
  • Action: a target cash share; the harness trades the difference, 5 bp per trade, 1-point dead band
  • The old BUY / SELL interface is kept behind a flag for the bridge cell
Why the start condition alone could produce the persona effect; now any allocation is reachable in one step
FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v210
Change 7 · targets

Where the target cash bands come from

Three kinds of source; each is used for one thing. The resulting bands are on the next slide.

1 · Practitioner conventions

set the levels
  • Fund companies publish standard conservative, balanced and aggressive portfolios.
  • Stocks: about a fifth, about half, almost all.
  • As cash: roughly 80 %, 50 % and 10–15 %.
SourcesMorningstar, US fund category definitions (2025)Vanguard LifeStrategy fundsFidelity model portfolios, methodologyBetterment, asset-allocation methodology

2 · Portfolio theory

rules out 100 % cash
  • Theory gives the stock share from how much risk a person can bear.
  • Even the most cautious investor holds some stocks (about 15–25 %).
  • No level of caution leads to 100 % cash.
SourcesDamodaran, equity risk premium data (2025)Vanguard, “A framework for allocating to cash” (2024)

3 · Personality finance & surveys

give the ordering, not the levels
  • Personality moves the stock share by only a few points: it fixes the order, not the levels.
  • Surveys: 25–40 points between the most and least cautious investors.
  • Used to check the ordering and report the spread.
SourcesJiang, Peng & Yan (2024), Journal of Financial EconomicsGilliam, Chatterjee & Grable (2010), J. Financial Counseling & PlanningFieberg et al. (2025), CESifo Working Paper 11666

The target cash bands, old and new

FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v212
Change 8

The prompt equals the table

  • The observation table in the paper is generated from the code: 19 fields, all of them rendered in the prompt
  • Portfolio state is included; horizon disclosure and field order are switchable factors
  • Every output row carries a hash of the generator configuration and of the prompt
  • Separate random streams per component, so a seed reproduces exactly across threads
Why paper, prompt and code cannot drift apart, and every run is traceable to its exact inputs

FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v214
Change 10

Evaluation with floors and ceilings

  • 11 rule-based baselines on the same path and start: always hold / buy / sell, random, buy-and-hold, constant mix, momentum, mean reversion, value oracle, mandate-conditional oracle, observables oracle
  • Steps with |mispricing| below 5 % are not scored; there is no right answer there
  • New score, mandate-conditional regret: distance to the best cash share inside the persona's band given the true mispricing
Why the old rationality score rated buy-and-hold near perfect (the floor sat above the ceiling); every number now has a reference point
FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v215

Additions beyond fixing shortcomings

  1. A fourth regime, sustained bull: rising value with no mispricing, a control for ‘is it a bubble or just a bull market?’
  2. Control arms: two placebos, wrapper-only, swapped mandate, and a trader with no mandate
  3. Stateful arms: rolling window, full transcript, and summary memory, with context length logged
  4. Multi-asset-capable generator: a three-asset configuration for allocation across holdings
  5. Design factors: trading costs (5 bp, visible or hidden), horizon disclosure, and field order
  6. Restatement probe: ‘repeat your mandate’ asked without trading, to separate memory from behaviour
  7. Baselines and an oracle inside the environment, plus a regret score with floors and ceilings
  8. A statistics track: model-level contrasts, mixed-effects models, multiple-testing correction
  9. Provenance: a configuration and prompt hash on every output row; the observation table is generated from code
FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v216
Addition 1

A fourth regime: the sustained bull

  • Value drifts up 0.15–0.25 % a day; there is no scripted mispricing, so price tracks value
  • From the price alone it looks like the start of a bubble, but there is nothing to sell
  • Rejection sampling keeps only paths that stay inside the control's validity band; the rejection rate is published
Why it separates ‘bubble’ from ‘bull market’: an agent that follows its mandate should stay invested here and step back in the bull trap
FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v217
Addition 2

Stateful arms and the restatement probe

  • Three ways of remembering; the mandate sits in the system prompt in all of them
  • Restatement probe: a forked call asks ‘state your mandate’ every k steps; the answer is logged and the trading trajectory is untouched
  • Each stateful arm has a stateless twin on the same seed, so memory is the only difference
Why it tells apart remembering the mandate from being reminded of it, and shows whether context length itself changes behaviour

FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v218
Addition 3

A multi-asset-capable generator

  • Three assets: two at full volatility, one at half; a common factor (ρ = 0.3) links their shocks
  • Each asset has its own value and mispricing; the agent sets a cash share and weights across assets
  • Oracle: cash follows ‘is any asset cheap or dear?’; weights are scored by distance to the best allocation
  • Leakage audits run on the full asset vector, using an asset's own block as the control
Why it moves the test from ‘how much cash’ to ‘which holding’ without changing the rules of the game

FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v220
Addition 5

A statistics track

QuestionMethod
Does the arm change the allocation?model-level contrasts with Cliff's δ and Hedges g; Benjamini–Hochberg correction across models
Is it the persona, or just that run?mixed-effects model with a random intercept per run; the static arm is the reference
Is it time, or the market phase?25-day window means with phase and time in one model; circular-shift null for phase-free runs
Does memory matter beyond the phase?paired sign-flip test: stateful minus stateless on the same seed
Is the persona even there on day 1?separability gate (ordering, effect size, band-hit rate) before any drift is scored
  • Reports and tables are generated from the run files, so the numbers in the paper come from code
Why every headline number now has a null, an effect size and a multiplicity correction behind it

FinPersona-Bench · synthetic market environment v226

Summary

  1. Ground truth is explicit; valuation-field leakage is fixed; phases are randomised; volatility is real
  2. Target cash bands are grounded in practitioner conventions and portfolio theory, with sources
  3. Start allocation, action, costs and control arms are design factors, not accidents
  4. Added: a sustained-bull control regime, stateful arms with a restatement probe, a multi-asset generator, a statistics track
  5. Baselines, a non-degenerate score and pre-registered checks; every failure is reported
  6. The pilot exercises every piece end to end
